title: El porqué de las naranjas

description.main: El porqué de las naranjas is Ricardo Cases's photographic survey of the Levante coast of Spain, a region of orange groves, holiday construction and weevil-stripped palms that he treats as a laboratory for the hidden mechanics of everyday life.
description.extended:
El porqué de las naranjas is Ricardo Cases's photographic survey of the Levante coast of Spain, a region of orange groves, holiday construction and weevil-stripped palms that he treats as a laboratory for the hidden mechanics of everyday life.

MACK published the book in October 2014 as a small white hardcover of 128 pages. A single picture is pasted to the front board: a palm trunk framed by painted yellow and orange struts. Inside, 67 colour photographs sit one to a spread, each with a wide margin and a blank facing page. The sequence moves from washed-out skies and crumbling resort architecture to recurring oranges, flames and scraps of colour that read like flags. Cases made the work after moving to Valencia following two bereavements. He calls it a portrait not of Levante but of its spirit, and through it of Spain after the 2008 crash. There is no essay. Photo-eye named it one of its Best Books of 2014.

Cases, born in Orihuela in 1971, trained as a journalist and joined the Blank Paper collective in 2006. His books include Paloma al aire (2011), El blanco (2016), Sol (2017) and Estudio elemental del Levante (2020), which returns to the same coast. The library also holds Paloma al aire.
description.artist_bio: Ricardo Cases (born Orihuela, Spain, 1971) studied information sciences at the University of the Basque Country and worked as a journalist before turning to photography. A member of the Blank Paper collective from 2006, he photographs the customs, subcultures and landscapes of provincial Spain. His photobooks include Belleza de barrio (2008), La caza del lobo congelado (2009), Paloma al aire (2011), El porqué de las naranjas (MACK, 2014), El blanco (Dalpine, 2016), Sol (Dalpine, 2017) and Estudio elemental del Levante (Dalpine, 2020).
